newsitem.title: UK: Hodder Headline hardback sales improve.
newsitem.headline: Hodder Headline hardback sales improve.

text.p: Sales of hardback fiction have benefited from the demise of a price-fixing cartel between publishers, Hodder Headline chief executive Tim Hely Hutchinson said on Tuesday.

"The biggest beneficiary of the Net Book Agreement (NBA) going is hardback fiction," Hely Hutchinson told Reuters, adding that sales of hardback fiction by the company's top authors such as Stephen King had doubled or trebled.
The NBA was a century-old pact under which publishers wcould fix the price of a title for six months from publication. It collapsed when a number of leading publishers withdrew.
Hely Hutchinson said that Hodder Headline had supported abolition of the NBA and added that, some 18 months after its collapse, virtually nobody in the trade mourned its passing.
He said that there were signs of an improvement in the British retail market after a difficult two years or so in which chains have cut their stock levels and closed stores.
"I hope we are ready to see an upswing," he said. However, the company has made its 1997 plans on the basis that educational and consumer book markets will not show significant growth over the year.
Hodder Headline's UK consumer publishing arm is looking for a boost from new deals with mystery writer Elizabeth George and James Patterson.
Stephen King has also moved his Dark Tower series, previously published elsewhere, to join the majority of his work at the Hodder & Stoughton imprint.
Hodder Headline operates in the UK and English speaking countries such as Australia, New Zealand and South Africa but not in the United States.
"One day we would like to have a subsidiary in the U.S. but right now we're rather glad we haven't," said Hely Hutchinson, noting tough conditions in the UK retail market.
But he said the U.S. unit was only a "long-range target" at this stage.
